text.title: Fox
text.menu_sub: Stalk hares, pounce, rest in your den.
text.intro_safe: Safe mode: explore! Play tag with the hares.
text.intro_survival: Hunt to stay fed. Rest in a den at night.
text.intro_wild: Other foxes guard their land. Keep your distance!
text.night_hint: It's night. Dig a den into a hillside and sleep in it.
text.too_exposed: Too exposed to sleep! Dig a den into a hillside and sleep in it.
text.hungry: You're hungry. Look for voles and hares, beetles, or berry bushes.
text.no_food: Nothing to eat here. Look for voles and hares, beetles, or berry bushes.
text.dig: Digging... (a den keeps you safe and warm)
text.rain_start: It's starting to rain. Shelter in a den to stay warm.
text.chased: A rival fox is chasing you off its land!
text.safe_tag: Tag, you got it! In Safe mode foxes fill up on berries.
text.rival_bite: A rival fox bit you! Run!
text.rival_caught_you: You were caught by a rival fox
text.about_looks: Orange-red fur, a white chest and a big bushy tail with a white tip. About as big as a medium-sized dog.
text.about_food: Mostly voles and mice. Also hares, birds, eggs, insects and lots of berries in autumn.
text.about_home: Sleeps curled up in the open with its tail over its nose. It uses a den only to raise its cubs.
text.about_winter: Stays awake all winter. It hears voles moving under the snow and pounces on them nose first.
text.about_young: Cubs are born in a den in April or May. Both parents bring them food.
text.about_fact: A fox wraps its bushy tail around itself like a warm blanket when it sleeps.
text.family_mother: Here's your mom! She knows every path in the forest.
text.family_father: And here's your dad. He brings home the food, so stay close!
text.family_siblings: These are your brothers and sisters. Expect lots of play-fighting!
text.family_you: And this little fluffball is you! Follow Mom and Dad to learn how to survive in Animundo.
text.lesson_eat: Mom found berries. Go and eat some too!
text.lesson_pounce: Mom is sneaking up on a hare. Creep closer and tap Pounce!
text.lesson_shelter: Back to the den! Follow Mom inside.
text.lesson_sleep: Time for a nap. Curl up in the den and tap Sleep.
text.fed_mother: Mom brought you a vole! +{food} food
text.fed_father: Dad brought you a vole! +{food} food
text.calling_mother: Mom is calling you. Stay close!
text.calling_father: Dad is calling you. Stay close!
text.bedtime: It's getting dark. The family is going back to the den. Come home and sleep!
text.grown_up: You're grown up! Time to find your own place in the forest.

year.shelter: Sleeps curled up in the open, tail over the nose. Digs or takes over a den (often an old badger sett) only to raise cubs.
year.young: Cubs born in the den in April–May.

food.spring: Voles, hares, birds and their eggs.
food.winter: Voles caught by hearing them under the snow and pouncing, and carrion.

year.notes: The winter 'mousing pounce' through the snow is a great thing to show.
